briefs.headline: Liverpool and Chelsea drawn together in the Carabao Cup fourth round
briefs.summary: Wednesday's draw sends Chelsea to Anfield in the week of Oct. 26, the club's first away tie in the competition this season after beating Luton and Leeds; Liverpool beat Tottenham 3-1 on Tuesday to get there. Arsenal go to League Two Fleetwood, Everton host Newcastle and Bradford host Peterborough.

briefs.headline: Burrow limited with a back injury but says he will play at Houston
briefs.summary: Wednesday's report listed Joe Burrow as limited with back tightness; he threw lightly in individual drills and said "I'll do what it takes to be out there." B.J. Hill rested and Shemar Stewart (knee) practiced fully, while Houston's Jadeveon Clowney (knee) and Jake Hummel (groin) did not practice. Kickoff is Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Reds beat the Dodgers 6-2 after Snell leaves in the first inning
briefs.summary: Elly De La Cruz's two-run homer, his 28th, and Dane Myers' seventh led a 13-hit night Wednesday at Great American Ball Park; Blake Snell left after one inning with left groin tightness. Tejay Antone won in relief, and Los Angeles stranded 12 runners and went 0 for 11 with runners in scoring position.

briefs.headline: Teven Jenkins sits out Browns practice with a back injury
briefs.summary: The guard listed first at right guard on the Week 2 depth chart did not practice Wednesday, and centers Parker Brailsford (thumb) and Elgton Jenkins (back), tackle Dawand Jones (head) and defensive tackle Maliek Collins (quad) were limited. Tampa Bay had Miles Killebrew (concussion) and Jacob Parrish (back) limited for Sunday's 1 p.m. ET game.

briefs.headline: Crew beat Orlando City 2-1 to reach the U.S. Open Cup final
briefs.summary: Josef Martinez scored at the back post from a Santiago Rodriguez corner in the ninth minute Wednesday at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field, Martin Ojeda leveled in the 40th and Brais Mendez finished Rodriguez's lobbed pass in the 52nd before 8,805. Columbus hosts St. Louis City on Oct. 21, its first final since 2010.

briefs.headline: Marshall expects Del Rio-Wilson back for Saturday at Missouri State
briefs.summary: Carlos Del Rio-Wilson, who left early in the first half against Middle Tennessee with an injury, is expected to return, the Herald-Dispatch reported Thursday; Tony Gibson said "Carlos sees the picture. If it's there, he takes his throws." Both teams have one win and one loss, and kickoff in Springfield, Mo., is 6:30 p.m. ET on CBS Sports Network.

briefs.headline: Hauser says Ohio must control the run at South Alabama
briefs.summary: South Alabama has rushed for 423 yards in two games, and John Hauser said "any time you can control the line of scrimmage and run the ball, it's good"; Ohio played Jacksonville State without two quarterbacks because of injuries. Safety Eli Thompson, KJ Sejour and lineman CJ Dawson II "will be back at some point this year," he said.

briefs.headline: Brewers beat the Pirates 5-4 on Yelich's two-run double
briefs.summary: Brandon Lowe's 31st homer, Oneil Cruz's 19th and Rafael Flores Jr.'s ninth had Pittsburgh ahead through six innings Wednesday at PNC Park before Christian Yelich doubled in two off Carmen Mlodzinski in the seventh. Antonio Senzatela won and Trevor Megill earned his 28th save; the Pirates had 12 hits.

briefs.headline: Rodriguez says Strachan could make his WVU debut against Virginia
briefs.summary: The 6-foot-5 Boise State transfer receiver has not played because of injury and "has been practicing a little bit," Rich Rodriguez said; running back Chris Talley (hamstring) is out one to two more weeks and JaCorey Thomas' eligibility hearing is Thursday. WVU has thrown 26 passes in two games ahead of Saturday's 7:30 p.m. ET game in Charlotte.

briefs.headline: Mitoumi pushes out Kotozakura and leaves the Aki basho with no unbeaten man
briefs.summary: Maegashira Mitoumi, 33, drove the ozeki (champion) out by oshidashi (push-out) on Day 5 at Ryogoku Kokugikan on Thursday, beating Kotozakura for the second straight tournament; Kotozakura, the last man without a loss, is four wins and one loss. Mitoumi is also four and one, and Sports Hochi said he pulled level with the leaders.

briefs.headline: Onosato, Kirishima and Atamifuji win on Day 5 as Aonishiki loses again
briefs.summary: Yokozuna (grand champion) Onosato forced out winless Yoshinofuji by yorikiri (force-out) on Thursday, Kirishima, chasing yokozuna promotion, sent out Takanosho, and sekiwake (junior champion) Atamifuji pushed out komusubi (fourth rank) Daieisho; all three are four wins and one loss. Ozeki (champion) Aonishiki was pushed down by Gonoyama and is three and two. Kyodo said nine men share the lead at one loss.

briefs.headline: Onosato draws Gonoyama on Day 6 as Kotozakura meets Takanosho
briefs.summary: Friday's card in Tokyo, ending early Friday ET, sends the yokozuna (grand champion) against the maegashira who pushed down Aonishiki; Aonishiki meets sekiwake (junior champion) Fujinokawa, Kirishima draws winless Yoshinofuji and Atamifuji faces Kotoshoho. Fujinokawa pushed out new komusubi (fourth rank) Hakunofuji on Thursday and is three wins and two losses; Hoshoryu, Wakatakakage and Wakanokatsu are listed kyujo (absent).

briefs.headline: Guardians beat the White Sox 6-3 and take sole possession of the AL Central lead
briefs.summary: Petey Halpin's three-run homer capped a four-run sixth at Progressive Field on Wednesday after Tommy Pham's three-run shot had put Chicago ahead; Parker Messick struck out eight over six innings and Cade Smith earned his 37th save. Cleveland leads Chicago by a half-game with nine games left, its first sole hold on the division since July 3.

briefs.headline: Crow-Armstrong homers twice as the Cubs beat the Braves 8-4
briefs.summary: Pete Crow-Armstrong hit his 43rd and 44th home runs and a triple at Wrigley Field on Wednesday, a franchise record for a left-handed hitter, and Shota Imanaga struck out eight over six innings of one-run ball. Chicago stays a half-game ahead of Philadelphia, which beat Washington behind Zack Wheeler, for the first NL wild card.

briefs.headline: Twins beat the Yankees 5-4 in 13 innings on Caratini's pinch-hit single
briefs.summary: Victor Caratini's single up the middle scored Luke Keaschall from second in Minneapolis on Wednesday; New York struck out 17 times, a season high, and hit into four double plays. The Yankees are 4.5 games behind Tampa Bay, which beat the Athletics 4-3 as Nick Martinez won his 15th.

briefs.headline: Seahawks rule Darnold out for Arizona and start Drew Lock
briefs.summary: Coach Mike Macdonald said Wednesday that Sam Darnold, who left the opener after five plays with what the team calls a glute soft-tissue injury, will not play Sunday and that he does not anticipate placing him on injured reserve. Lock, who relieved Darnold in the win over New England, starts with Jalen Milroe as the backup.

briefs.headline: Murray practices on a limited basis as the Vikings weigh his status for Chicago
briefs.summary: Kyler Murray, concussed on a hard hit while sliding 11 snaps into Sunday's win over Green Bay, was limited at Wednesday's practice while still in the league's protocol. "We'll see how he responds and continue to rely on the medical folks," coach Kevin O'Connell said; Carson Wentz would start at Soldier Field if Murray is not cleared.

briefs.headline: Brighton beat Manchester United 3-2 from two goals down in the Carabao Cup
briefs.summary: Shea Lacey and Mason Mount scored in the eighth and ninth minutes at Old Trafford on Wednesday before Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper answered, putting United out at the first hurdle for a second straight season. "We can't accept that as a group. I take responsibility for it," Michael Carrick said.

briefs.headline: Everton beat Wolves 1-0 and Villa win at Coventry as the third round nears its end
briefs.summary: Everton beat Wolverhampton 1-0, Aston Villa won 3-1 at Coventry and League Two Fleetwood beat Sheffield United 1-0 on Wednesday. Manchester City host Norwich on Thursday at 2:30 p.m. ET (7:30 p.m. BST) in the last third-round tie.

briefs.headline: NCAA committee says clock error decided Michigan's 13-12 win over Western Michigan
briefs.summary: The FBS Oversight Committee said Wednesday the Week 1 result "would have been different" had officials not added one second before Bryce Underwood's 47-yard touchdown pass to JJ Buchanan, but that it has no authority to overturn a game. The MAC's appeal to have Western Michigan declared the winner was denied, and the NCAA issued new timing guidance.

sections.label: In Season

coming_in.item: Two days out. The migratory bird summary, downloaded and read again this morning, lists Saturday, Sept. 19, and Oct. 31 as the two single youth waterfowl days for ducks, geese, coots, gallinules and mergansers, open to hunters under 18; footnote (b) sets the youth-day bag at the daily limit of the regular duck and goose seasons, except that two scaup may be taken as part of the six-duck daily bag. Hunters under 15 must be accompanied by a licensed adult 18 or older who may not hunt or carry a firearm, only nontoxic shot size T or smaller may be in the hunter's possession, shooting hours are one-half hour before sunrise to sunset, and every licensed hunter needs a HIP registration card. The same table opens the regular duck season Oct. 3-11 at six a day and 18 in possession under footnotes (c) and (d), with coots on the duck dates at 15 and 45.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary, September 2026 - January 2027

coming_in.item: Two days out. The second gun window for bear runs Saturday, Sept. 19, through Sept. 25 in SELECTED COUNTIES, a list the summary table does not carry, so no county is named here; the county-by-county rules and limits are on pamphlet pages 33-39 and vary by permit class. Electronic registration is required. The next gun windows are Oct. 3-9 and Oct. 22-25.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

coming_in.item: Nine days out. Archery and crossbow seasons for deer and for bear both open Saturday, Sept. 26, and run through Dec. 31, with electronic registration required for each; the deer and bear bag limits are not in the summary table at all, only on pamphlet pages 13-18 and 33-39, and are not printed here. Wild boar archery and crossbow opens the same day, one a season.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

coming_in.item: Sixteen days out. The migratory bird summary's next goose date is Saturday, Oct. 3, the first of three splits, five a day and 15 in possession in aggregate under footnote (d), with snow and blue geese on the same dates and limits. Shooting hours are one-half hour before sunrise to sunset, and HIP registration is required. At McClintic and Green Bottom wildlife management areas, waterfowl hours run only until noon Oct. 3-11, the McClintic controlled area is by permit in that window, and concurrent hunting is prohibited there on those dates.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary, September 2026 - January 2027

prime.item: Day 6. The general squirrel season opened Saturday, Sept. 12, and runs through Feb. 28, and the summary table sets the daily bag at six and the possession limit at 24, with no season limit and no registration requirement.
prime.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

prime.item: The first dove segment is in its 17th day with 24 days left after today, running through Oct. 11, with a daily bag of 15 and a possession limit of 45, per the migratory bird summary read again this morning; shooting hours are one-half hour before sunrise to sunset for the rest of the segment, and HIP registration is required. Sora and Virginia rails run Sept. 1 to Nov. 9, 10 a day and 30 in possession in aggregate, and Wilson's snipe Sept. 1 to Dec. 16, eight and 24, on the same table; woodcock does not open until Oct. 17.
prime.publication: West Virginia Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary, September 2026 - January 2027

prime.item: The Marine Fisheries recreational limits page, effective Sept. 2 and opened again this morning, holds red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length, one a day, under federal red drum management. The Fisherman's Post September report, published Sept. 1 and 16 days old with nothing newer on the feed this morning, has Native Son working drum at docks and creek mouths on topwater early and deeper presentations and natural bait as the sun rises, Speckled Specialist finding reds in small groups around oysters, docks, grass points and ledges, Carolina Flats on morning topwater, Spring Tide reporting over-slot fish of 28 to 32 inches and river drum early and late, and Jolly Roger Pier taking red drum in the bottom fishing.

Limits page: 14 to 20 inches total length, three a day, one of the three allowed over 26 inches. Speckled Specialist's Sept. 1 paragraph in the Fisherman's Post says trout numbers vary trip to trip, Jolly Roger Pier had them in the bottom fishing and Surf City Pier early and in the evening; a 16-day-old monthly report, not this morning's water.

Limits page: Spanish 12-inch fork length, 15 a day; bluefish no minimum, and footnote M sets the creel at three per person per day in private recreational fishing and five aboard a for-hire vessel. East Coast Sports' Sept. 1 paragraph had both on casting jigs early, Jolly Roger Pier had them on plugs and sight casting early and late, Surf City Pier had Spanish on Gotcha plugs and casting jigs, and Spring Tide and South End had bigger Spanish over live bottom and hard bottom offshore, 16 days ago.

Limits page: black drum 14-inch minimum and 25-inch maximum total length, 10 a day; sheepshead 14 inches total length, five a day. The Fisherman's Post Sept. 1 report, 16 days old, has black drum in the bottom fishing at both Jolly Roger and Surf City piers, with pompano and croakers, and does not mention sheepshead this month.

sections.note: Nothing on either state's calendar closes within two weeks: North Carolina's recreational flounder harvest ended Sept. 14 and the Marine Fisheries limits page, opened this morning, still prints 'Sep 15-30: CLOSED, unlawful to possess', with no other species on the page carrying a September or October closing date; West Virginia's early Canada goose season closed Sept. 13 and the first dove segment has 24 days to run. Gauley Fest opens today, Thursday, Sept. 17, and runs through Sunday, Sept. 20, at Nicholas County Veterans Memorial Park in Summersville, per American Whitewater's event page, opened this morning, which gives 8 a.m. Thursday to noon Sunday; the organization's Gauley page gives a different Thursday schedule, vendor registration at 10 a.m. and the campground at noon, with 6 a.m. river releases Friday, Saturday and Sunday, so no Thursday hour is printed. The second Gauley release window opens tomorrow, Friday, Sept. 18, and runs through Monday, Sept. 21: the National Park Service's whitewater page for the Gauley River, last updated Aug. 26, answered this morning and lists the Corps of Engineers' planned Summersville Lake releases as Sept. 11-14, 18-21 and 25-28 and Oct. 2-5, 9-12 and 17-18. The Monongahela alerts page, opened this morning, carries nothing dated Sept. 15, 16 or 17: the Sept. 14 Forest Road 19 Dolly Sods closure, the Sept. 8 Forest Road 76 closure on the Gauley district, the Aug. 12 Tea Creek Campground bridge alert and the July 17 Forest Road 86-Williams River closure stand. A search for WVDNR trout stocking in September 2026 found no notice and the division's stocking page, which answered only through a fetch after refusing curl, lists no entry, so nothing is printed. The WV hunting reference file is valid through June 30, 2027, and was checked against today's date.

sections.label: On the Water

waters.reading: 58.8 cfs, 1.37 feet, falling, four days off the Sunday-evening crest.
waters.working: Down 14.1 cfs and a tenth of a foot from the 72.9 and 1.47 this paper printed at this hour Wednesday, and the recession has gone flat: the USGS two-day trace, pulled at 5:45 a.m., runs from 105 cfs and 1.66 feet at 5:45 a.m. Tuesday through 87.0 at 5:45 p.m., 77.4 at 1:45 a.m. Wednesday, 72.9 at 5:15, 69.9 at 9:15, 67.0 at 1:15 p.m., 64.2 at 5:15, 62.8 at 9:15, 61.5 at midnight, 60.1 at 1:15 a.m. and 58.8 from 3:30 to 5:15 this morning, about six-tenths of a cfs an hour now against 1.3 yesterday. The fetcher's falling flag compares against Tuesday morning's 105.0 and 1.66, the first point of the two-day trace, and agrees with the trace. At 58.8 cfs the river is 2.6 cfs and two-hundredths of a foot over the 56.2 and 1.35 this paper printed for Sunday morning before the rain, so the pockets are back to base and this is the long-leader, small-fly problem in full: caddis, stoneflies and sculpin are the forage, and pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks the structure, which at this flow means a 12-foot leader tapered to 6X, a size 16 to 18 caddis dry or elk-hair emerger fished up through the pocket heads and the tailouts of the plunge pools, a size 16 or 18 stonefly nymph or pheasant tail dropped a foot under it in the few seams still carrying current, and a small olive sculpin swung tight under the undercut banks before the light is on the water, because at 1.37 feet every fish in the pockets can see a shadow and a wading angler. NWS Charleston's forecast for Cowen, issued 5:37 a.m., has showers and thunderstorms likely after 9 a.m. at a 70% chance, partly sunny with a high near 80, a west wind around 5 and a tenth to a quarter of an inch of rain; a 50% chance continues tonight with a low around 64, and Friday carries a chance of showers before noon and storms in the afternoon with a high near 76. A quarter inch on a river at base will show on the gauge as color at the creek mouths before it shows as flow.
waters.note: No water temperature came back from the gauge this morning, so no warm-water trout line can be printed. The only NWS product active in West Virginia at 5:45 a.m. was a Special Weather Statement for heat, issued 5:12 a.m. by NWS Charleston, for heat indices in the mid-90s to near 100 this afternoon in the lowland counties from Wayne, Cabell and Mason through Putnam, Kanawha and Roane; Webster County is not on it. The Monongahela alerts page, opened this morning, still carries the July 17 notice closing Forest Road 86-Williams River from July 20 for flood-damage repair, the Aug. 12 Tea Creek Campground bridge alert, the Sept. 8 Forest Road 76 closure and the Sept. 14 Forest Road 19 order on the Dolly Sods side; nothing is dated Sept. 15, 16 or 17. The fetcher's 24-hour comparison on all three USGS gauges this morning reaches back to Tuesday 5:45 a.m., the first point of the two-day trace; its read string, 'prime wading water', is printed as written.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.92 feet, up 0.30 since Wednesday morning, easing off a 25.30 bump Wednesday evening.
waters.read: 24.9 ft and falling — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Up, not down, on the day: 0.30 over the 24.62 this paper printed at this hour Wednesday. The fetcher's 25.79 comparison is Tuesday morning's number, the first point of the two-day trace, and its falling flag describes only the last 11 hours. The trace bottomed at 24.38 feet at 8 a.m. Wednesday, then climbed all day: 24.68 at 10 a.m., 24.94 at noon, 25.17 at 3 p.m., 25.29 at 5 and 25.30 at 5:30 p.m., the top of the last 26 hours, before easing to 25.16 at 8 p.m., 25.09 at 10, 25.15 at midnight, 25.02 at 1 a.m., 24.94 at 3, 24.98 at 4 and 24.92 at 5, so it rose nine-tenths in nine hours, has given back four-tenths since supper and is holding within a tenth for the last four hours. The NWPS observation for POPW2 at 5 a.m. is 24.92, matching the USGS figure; the Weather Service's forecast for Point Pleasant, issued 10 a.m. Wednesday, had 24.4 at 6 a.m. today, 24.4 at noon, 24.5 by 6 p.m. and 24.6 to 24.7 through Saturday, and the river is half a foot over that whole curve. Action stage is 38 feet, so this is normal pool with a little fresh water moving through it. Shad, skipjack and crawfish are the forage, and wing dams, riprap, the lock wall and barge cuts the structure: with the pool flat and a hair over its forecast, the shad are on the current faces of the wing dams and off their tips in the little flow there is, so a white swimbait or a chartreuse-and-white spinnerbait across the upstream faces and off the tips, a black-and-blue jig with a crawfish trailer dragged down the riprap points, and a walking topwater over the barge cuts in the fog before 8 a.m., which NWS Charleston's forecast, issued 5:37 a.m., has as patchy fog before 8, then a 40% chance of showers and thunderstorms, mostly sunny with a high near 90 and a southwest wind of 1 to 6; tonight a chance of storms between 8 p.m. and 2 a.m. with a low around 69, and Friday rain showers likely before 8 a.m. at 60%, then partly sunny and 83.
waters.note: This is the pool side, 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam; USGS does not gauge the Byrd tailwater. The fetcher's falling flag is printed with its read string as written, and the 24-hour direction, up 0.30, is the trace's. NWS Charleston's Special Weather Statement for heat, issued 5:12 a.m., puts heat indices from the mid-90s to near 100 this afternoon into early evening across the lowland counties including Mason, Jackson, Putnam and Cabell; it names no end time. The NWPS forecast page for POPW2 still carries the Wednesday-morning curve the river is running half a foot over. The Corps' Huntington District site was not tried this morning and no lock notice is printed.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.48 feet, down 0.85 since Wednesday morning, off a 26.68 overnight bump.
waters.read: 26.5 ft and falling — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Down 0.85 from the 27.33 this paper printed at this hour Wednesday; the fetcher's 28.3 comparison is Tuesday morning's number, the first point of the two-day trace, and its falling flag agrees with the trace over 24 hours and over the last five, though not overnight. The river fell from 27.36 at 4 a.m. Wednesday to 27.11 at 7, 26.91 at 9, 26.59 at 11 a.m., 26.43 at 1 p.m. and a low of 26.16 at 5:15 p.m., then came back up half a foot through the evening, 26.36 at 6 p.m., 26.44 at 9, 26.53 at 10, 26.68 at midnight, 26.66 at 1 a.m., before easing again to 26.61 at 2, 26.55 at 3, 26.57 at 4 and 26.48 at 5. Point Pleasant, above the dam, put on nine-tenths Wednesday afternoon and that water is what showed up below the dam overnight. The NWPS observation for HNTW2 at 5 a.m. is 26.56, eight-hundredths above the USGS figure, and had 26.74 at 4:30; the Weather Service's forecast for Huntington, issued 10 a.m. Wednesday, had 26.0 at 2 a.m. today, 25.7 at 8 a.m., 25.6 by 2 p.m. and 25.5 from tonight through Saturday, so the river is running half a foot to eight-tenths over its curve, and action stage is 48 feet. Under a foot over the early-September pool and moving in both directions inside a day, the river fishes as the read says, normal pool, with the seams alive: shad and skipjack are the forage, and the eddies below the lock wall and behind the wing dams are where the little push overnight has stacked them, so a three-quarter-ounce white swimbait or a skipjack-pattern jerkbait along the seam where the eddy meets the flow for hybrids and white bass, and a crawfish-colored football jig dragged down the riprap where the drop is, is the bank cast; the fog before 9 a.m. is the cool water of the day. NWS Charleston's forecast for Huntington, issued 5:02 a.m., has patchy fog before 9 a.m., then a 50% chance of showers and thunderstorms, mostly sunny with a high near 94 and a heat index to 101, a west wind of 1 to 5, storms possible through 2 a.m. and a low around 71; Friday is partly sunny and 87 with showers possible before 11 a.m.
waters.note: This is the gauge below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam, not the tailwater. The fetcher's flag and read string say falling, and the trace agrees on the day, down 0.85 in 24 hours, and on the last five hours; the overnight rise from 26.16 to 26.68 sits inside that fall and is printed from the trace. NWS Charleston's Special Weather Statement for heat, issued 5:12 a.m., covers Cabell and Wayne counties this afternoon into early evening with heat indices from the mid-90s to near 100 and names no end time. The Corps' Huntington District site was not tried and no lock notice is printed.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: high 1:09 AM at 3.2 ft, low 7:13 AM at 0.9 ft, high 1:43 PM at 4.0 ft, low 8:11 PM at 1.3 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: high 11:58 PM (Wed) at 3.6 ft, low 5:48 AM at 0.9 ft, high 12:36 PM at 4.6 ft, low 7:08 PM at 1.3 ft. Water 80.6F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast. Moon waxing crescent, 31% lit, 5.5 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 1:09 AM and 1:43 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Spring tides easing toward neap: the moon is five and a half days past new and about two days short of first quarter, and the sound swings 3.1 feet from the 7:13 a.m. low to the 1:43 p.m. high, two-tenths less than Wednesday and four-tenths less than Tuesday, with 3.7 feet of range at the ocean station against 4.2 yesterday, so the inlet current is softening a notch each day and the afternoon high at 4.0 feet is a tenth lower than Wednesday's. The sound today runs 67 minutes behind the inlet on the midday high, 71 on the overnight high, and 85 and 63 minutes behind on the morning and evening lows, so the flood in the backwater runs from 7:13 a.m. to 1:43 p.m. and the afternoon ebb from 1:43 to 8:11 p.m. The morning low at 7:13 is slack, dead water at the inlet, and the first hour of the flood is the topwater window Native Son and Carolina Flats both described on Sept. 1, a walking plug along the grass edges and over the oyster bars at docks and creek mouths; as the water tops the bars toward 1:43 p.m., a gold spoon or a paddletail on a quarter-ounce head in the flooded grass, and a live shrimp under a popping cork over the deeper oyster edges and ledges for the trout that Speckled Specialist had scattered but present. The last of the ebb, roughly 6 to 8:11 p.m., is the red drum window on the tide preference that matters most here, shrimp and finger mullet draining out of the grass into the creek channels, and a cut mullet or a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig a couple of feet off the channel edge at a creek mouth, the mullet being thick by Carolina Flats' account; Spring Tide's over-slot fish of 28 to 32 inches are over the 27-inch maximum on the limits page and go back. Flounder are closed through Sept. 30 and unlawful to possess: the Carolina Flats one-ounce bucktail with a Gulp curly tail along the ICWW channel edges and dock pilings on the ebb finds them, and they go back too. After dark the flood from 8:11 p.m. pushes bait past the dock lights, and a small paddletail or shrimp imitation drifted through the edge of the light is the trout cast. Surf: the Weather Service's surf zone forecast for Coastal Pender, issued 2:31 a.m., has surf around 2 feet, a LOW rip current risk, northeast winds around 5 becoming east in the afternoon, sunny and mid 80s with water around 80 and a very high UV index, which is the calm-morning Spanish and bluefish setup from the reference pattern and the one East Coast Sports, Jolly Roger and Surf City reported on Sept. 1: a Gotcha plug or a casting jig under birds off the pier ends on the 5:48 a.m. low and into the flood, with the piers' bottom fishing for black drum, Virginia mullet, pompano and croakers the fallback through the 12:36 p.m. high.
waters.note: The Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry September report is 16 days old, published Tuesday, Sept. 1, at 10 a.m. ET, and the feed, opened at 5:50 a.m., carries nothing newer, so there is no new report; the article was re-opened this morning and it is the month's pattern, not this morning's water. All four sound events fall inside today, midnight to midnight, and the fetcher tagged no spillover in the sound; the surf's 11:58 PM high carries the fetcher's Wednesday tag and is last night's. No Beach Hazards Statement is active for Coastal Pender this morning, the first day since Monday without one, and the only NWS alert in North Carolina at 5:45 a.m. did not cover the coast. The surf zone forecast gives the Topsail Inlet high as 12:36 p.m., 67 minutes ahead of the sound today; Friday is a low rip risk with surf 1 to 3 feet and southwest winds 5 to 10, and Saturday through Monday are low. NWS Wilmington's point forecast for the island, issued 5:39 a.m., has sunny and 84 with an east wind around 7, mostly clear and 71 tonight with a southwest wind around 5, and 88 Friday with southwest 2 to 10 gusting to 16. The National Hurricane Center's 2 a.m. Atlantic outlook has no active systems and one area, a small low a few hundred miles east of Bermuda designated AL98, at 40% in 48 hours and 40% in seven days, up from 10 and 30 Wednesday, moving slowly west today and possibly turning south Friday over the subtropical Atlantic, nothing near the Carolinas. Hampstead is the sound station and the tide that matters. Water temperature is Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, not the sound.

sections.note: All four waters reported from out/fishing.json, fetched 5:32 a.m. and not re-run. The fetcher's 24-hour comparison on every USGS gauge this morning is Tuesday 5:45 a.m., the first point of the two-day trace; the Williams and Huntington falling flags agree with the traces on the day, but Point Pleasant's does not, the pool having risen nine-tenths through Wednesday afternoon to 25.30 and given back four-tenths since, so it stands 0.30 over Wednesday morning and its 24-hour direction is printed from the trace. Both Ohio gauges are running half a foot or more over the Weather Service's Wednesday-morning forecast curves at normal pool; the Williams is at 58.8 cfs, within 3 cfs of its pre-rain base, with rain likely at Cowen after 9 a.m. The only NWS product in West Virginia is a Special Weather Statement for heat indices to near 100 in the lowland counties this afternoon; there is no Beach Hazards Statement for Coastal Pender today and the rip current risk is low.

kicker: Nine men share the Aki basho lead at one loss after Day 5; the Crew host St. Louis City in the U.S. Open Cup final Oct. 21, and the second Gauley release window opens Friday.
